exposure: Maternal body mass index (adequate weight vs. overweight/obese) at the beginning of pregnancy
Maternal overweight and obesity during pregnancy and breastfeeding
outcome: Maternal health alterations (number of pregnancies, abortions, plasma glucose levels, prenatal control visits, plasma platelet levels)
Newborn growth (somatometric development, weight for age, length for age, weight for length classification)
Risk of the baby being overweight (weight for length indicator)
cohort: Forty-two healthy mother-child pairs (binomials) without problems during delivery and without serious illnesses during the breastfeeding period were included.
finding: Maternal overweight and obesity at the beginning of pregnancy were associated with a higher risk of the baby being overweight according to the weight-for-length indicator at 180 days, and with several negative maternal health outcomes.
